sn2.3:1.2: Māgha is one of the many names of Sakka. It’s a _taddhita_ construction from _magha_ in possessive sense meaning “bounteous one”, and is thus a synonym of Maghavā ([sn11.12:1.3]()).
sn2.3:3.4: _Vatrabhū_ is the Pali spelling of Sanskrit _vṛtrahan_, “slayer of the Constrictor”. Vṛtra was a massive cobra whose defeat at the hands of Indra/Sakka, was one of the primordial myths underlying the Vedas (eg. Rig Veda 1.32). Vṛtra, who was identified with wickedness (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 11.1.5.7), held the waters imprisoned. The release of the waters for the good of all is the primary symbol of Indra’s bounty.
